items.after:
- Add `INFECTION_DELAY` (seconds) as a named tuning constant in `src/main.js`.
- Mark a human infected when a zombie moves onto its cell (the only contact
  vector while humans are static). Track it as a per-human timer.
- Each tick, count infected humans' timers down by `dt()`; when one reaches
  zero, replace that human with a `Zombie` on the same cell — remove it from
  `humans`, push a new `Zombie` into `zombies`, and swap sprites (destroy the
  human's, render the zombie's).
- Make `humans` and `zombies` mutable so converted humans drop out of zombie
  targeting, which reads the live `humans` array.

Small observability aid: render infected humans with a distinct text color so
the timed conversion is visible in the browser before it fires.
items.before:
Zombies pursue the nearest human via `nextStepToward` (`src/map.js`) but nothing
happens on contact. In `src/main.js`, `humans` and `zombies` are `const` arrays
filtered from the spawn; humans never move yet (that's item 7) and carry no
infection state. Tuning values live as module-level `const`s in `main.js`.
